Olu to provide Helm chart example + deployment YAMLs by 2026-04-05
Schedule deep dive on SSO/KMS with Jonas for week of 2026-04-06
Helio to confirm target regions and billing model by 2026-04-08

summary: Partner integration sync covering marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for private/VPC deployments, joint solution packaging (Helm/chart + container), security considerations (KMS/SSO/SOC2), and next steps for co-marketing and technical artifacts.
transcript:
[00:00] Grace Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Grace from Redwood, I think we have about an hour, is that still good?
[00:05] Priya Sharma: Yep that's perfect, thanks Grace. Priya here at HelioMarket.
[00:10] Olu Martins: Hey all, Olu from Redwood infra SE, I'll run through the reference arch and the deployment bits.
[00:17] Luca Bianchi: Luca, platform eng at Helio, quick heads up we care a lot about VPC egress and private control plane for our regulated customers.
[00:25] Grace Kim: Great, that's actually top of agenda. We wanted to align on two tracks - marketplace listing requirements and the technical reference arch for private deployments and a packaged helm chart.
[00:35] Amara Diallo: From bizdev I just want to make sure timeline lines up with marketing - we want to be live in Q2.
[00:40] Grace Kim: Okay noted. We'll go through what we need for the vendor listing, the field mapping for billing, and then Olu will deep dive on deployment artefacts.
[00:48] Olu Martins: Cool. Slide-less, I'll just share screen with an exemplar ref-arch I sent earlier, hope that's visible - (screen shared sound).
[01:00] Olu Martins: So top-level, we have a marketplace integration that can route to either Redwood hosted env or a Private deployment in a customer VPC or on-prem. The main pieces are: control plane (Redwood), serving runtime (GPU nodes), ingress proxy, KMS/HSM integration for keys, and a connector for audit logs back to the customer's SIEM.
[01:22] Jonas Meyer: Quick Q - for KMS, do you support Bring Your Own Key? We have strict key separation.
[01:28] Sofia Alvarez: Short answer yes, BYOK for private deployments. For hosted we use Redwood-managed keys unless the customer requests KMS integration. There might be an extra entitlement for HSM.
[01:40] Luca Bianchi: And audit logs? We need to stream audit logs to Splunk.
[01:44] Olu Martins: We support streaming via syslog/HTTPS to partner SIEMs, plus S3 archival. We'll include example Fluentd configs in the repo.
[01:55] Priya Sharma: On the marketplace listing side, what's required? We saw the marketplace has spec fields for billing - metering by token or per-request?
[02:03] Grace Kim: Good point. For listing we normally provide both options: per-invocation metering (e.g., per-request or per-concurrency) and per-token billing for hosted. Marketplace typically expects a billing descriptor and SKU mapping - Olu can provide the sample mapping.
[02:18] Olu Martins: Yeah we have a spreadsheet that maps Redwood pricing to marketplace SKUs, and we'll share that. The important metadata fields are billing_unit, sku_id, region_availability, and support_contact.
[02:30] Amara Diallo: Any special requirements for co-branding assets? We need logos, one-liner, and a 60-90 sec demo clip.
[02:37] Grace Kim: We'll share a co-branding checklist. Marketing will also need a short product blurb and a demo video - we can supply a template video if you want.
[02:45] Priya Sharma: On the technical side - for reference architectures, can you walk through the private deployment flow?
[02:50] Olu Martins: Sure. Customer provisions VPC and subnets, we deploy a control-plane helm release into a management namespace that talks to the Redwood console; for Private deployments the control plane can be self-hosted or we can run a managed control plane within the partner account. The serving nodes remain inside customer VPC, behind private IGWs. KV cache persists to an encrypted EBS or equivalent, and model artifacts are pulled from an S3-compatible object store with signed roles.
[03:20] Luca Bianchi: Signed roles - so IAM role chaining? We use federated roles in our infra.
[03:24] Olu Martins: Yes, we support IRSA/assumed roles and short-term creds. We can provide an IAM trust policy example.
[03:30] Jonas Meyer: About network egress - do you force outbound to Redwood endpoints? Some customers require egress restrictions.
[03:36] Sofia Alvarez: We support an air-gapped mode too for on-prem; for VPC installs we can route telemetry to customer endpoints and block public egress. There are trade-offs - e.g., model pulls and updates require a controlled egress window or pre-staged artifacts.
[03:52] Priya Sharma: That trade-off is okay for our enterprise customers as long as updates are planned.
[03:58] Grace Kim: Great. Next, packaging - we usually provide a Helm chart and a reference container image. Olu, can you describe the chart layout?
[04:05] Olu Martins: The chart uses a main values.yaml with sections: replica counts, GPU instance class, autoscaler config, resource quotas, KV cache config, and quantization/FP flags. We also provide kustomize overlays for region-specific settings. We'll include an example values file for Helio with recommended sizes.
[04:24] Luca Bianchi: For GPU drivers and CUDA compatibility, do you require specific AMIs or images?
[04:29] Olu Martins: We recommend using our validated AMI list or a container runtime that supports nvidia-container-toolkit. We'll include a driver matrix. For GKE/AKS we have node-pool recommendations.
[04:41] Amara Diallo: From commercial side is there a preferred go-to-market bundle? We want a joint solution page and a marketplace listing that routes to a trial.
[04:50] Grace Kim: Yes, the typical flow is marketplace listing -> trial entitlement -> self-serve credit -> paid upgrade or Reserved capacity. We'll coordinate with billing to map the entitlement.
[04:59] Priya Sharma: Any gotchas for the marketplace review process? We've seen long reviews at other vendors.
[05:04] Grace Kim: Checklist: security questionnaire (we'll prefill), SOC2 artifacts, scannable container images, CVE scans, and a short integration test script. Also the listing needs support SLAs and contact emails. We'll prep those.
[05:20] Jonas Meyer: On the security questionnaire - can you share your pen-test and SOC2 dates?
[05:24] Grace Kim: We'll attach the most recent SOC2 report and pen-test summary. We rotate every 12 months, next due late 2026 Q3.
[05:33] Olu Martins: Also note for private installs we can enable customer side auditing and key access logs to meet compliance needs.
[05:40] Priya Sharma: Great. Anything about latency SLAs for curated models?
[05:44] Sofia Alvarez: For Dedicated tenants we provide latency targets and SLOs per model class. We'll include benchmark artifacts. For marketplace we'll specify expected latency ranges per region.
[05:55] Grace Kim: Alright, let's capture next steps - we'll send the marketplace checklist, the ref-arch diagram, and a sample Helm repo. Also schedule the SSO/KMS deep dive with Jonas.
[06:06] Amara Diallo: Sounds good. Also, can Redwood help with a short co-badged webinar?
[06:10] Grace Kim: Absolutely, we can work marketing to schedule a joint webinar after listing goes live.
[06:15] Priya Sharma: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[06:18] Grace Kim: Thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts. 
[06:22] [call ends]
